title: Choose and evaluate models · Level 3
slo: Choose a model approach for a task and explain how Foundry evaluates models.

exercises.question_text: Which model is described as an Anthropic frontier-level model?

options.rationale: Claude Opus 4.5 is described as an Anthropic frontier-level model. It is intended for sophisticated agents and difficult reasoning tasks.
GPT-5.x is optimized for reasoning, planning, and agentic workflows. It is not the Anthropic model named here.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-5.x for structured logic, multi-step reasoning, and adjustable thinking levels.

feedback.intrinsic: A team needing the stated Anthropic option would begin evaluating the wrong family.
feedback.instructional: Keep the model names distinct: Claude Opus 4.5 is the Anthropic frontier-level choice.

options.error_type: Confuses general-purpose model with frontier agent model
options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 is a general-purpose model that balances quality, throughput, cost, and latency. It is not described as Anthropic’s frontier-level model.
options.better_fit: Choose Mistral Large 3 for balanced multilingual drafting or business-report work.

feedback.intrinsic: The selection would emphasize balance rather than the specified frontier-level capability.
feedback.instructional: Mistral Large 3 is a different model with a different focus. The Anthropic frontier-level model is Claude Opus 4.5.

options.error_type: Confuses real-time chat model with frontier model
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is optimized for responsive, high-volume chat. It is not the Anthropic frontier-level model.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for real-time chat, customer support, and interactive applications.

feedback.intrinsic: The choice would favor fast scale instead of the requested sophisticated-agent work.
feedback.instructional: GPT-4.1 and Claude Opus 4.5 solve different needs. The latter is the frontier-level Anthropic option.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Claude Opus 4.5 is the Anthropic frontier-level model in this set.

exercises.question_text: A designer is building a campaign tool where people can send images, audio, and video in a chat. Which models can fit this feature? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Phi-4-multimodal-instruct is listed for multimodal work. This task includes images, audio, and video in chat.
GPT-5.x chat multimodal is listed as a multimodal option. It can support chat completions involving images, audio, and video.
Mistral Large 3 is listed as a multimodal option. It can fit chat completions that use images, audio, and video.
text-embedding-3-small is built for semantic vector representations. It is not listed as a model for multimodal chat completions.
options.better_fit: Choose text-embedding-3-small for search or comparison by meaning.

feedback.intrinsic: The campaign chat would lack a model type selected for its image, audio, and video inputs.
feedback.instructional: Use a multimodal model for chat with images, audio, and video. Use embeddings for semantic vector representations.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The selected models are listed for multimodal chat involving images, audio, and video.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A reader could miss how Mistral Large 3 combines quality and throughput for general-purpose work.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the model, then state its strong quality, efficient throughput, and general-purpose use.

exercises.correct_answer: Mistral Large 3 offers strong quality with efficient throughput for general-purpose use
exercises.explanation: This order forms a grammatical statement that matches the source description of Mistral Large 3 as a general-purpose model offering strong quality with efficient throughput.

exercises.question_text: A legal-services team needs an industry-specific assistant. A second team needs search that finds content by meaning. Which choices fit these two needs? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Domain-tuned catalog models can fit legal applications. This directly meets the industry-specific requirement.

options.text: Use an embedding model for search
options.rationale: Embedding models create semantic vector representations. That supports search based on meaning.
text-embedding-3-small is listed as an embedding model. It is a fitting choice for semantic vector representations.

options.error_type: Confuses chat model with embedding task
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is optimized for real-time chat and customer support. It is not the listed embedding-model choice.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for fast, efficient interactive chat at scale.

feedback.intrinsic: The search team could choose a chat-focused model instead of the model type designed to represent meaning.
feedback.instructional: Separate the tasks: legal specialization points to a domain-tuned model, while semantic search points to an embedding model.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Domain-tuned models fit industry-specific work, while embedding models support search by meaning.

exercises.question_text: A research analyst needs an agent to work through extended notes, reason about complex code, and complete multi-step computer-use tasks. Which model is the strongest fit?

options.rationale: Claude Opus 4.5 fits extended notes through its large context window. It is also described for complex code reasoning and multi-step computer use.

options.error_type: Confuses reasoning orchestration with Claude's long-context computer-use fit
options.rationale: GPT-5.x is strong for reasoning, structured logic, planning, and agentic workflows. The full set of needs here specifically matches Claude Opus 4.5.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-5.x for technical reports, code analysis, and multi-capability agent orchestration.

feedback.intrinsic: The analyst might get strong reasoning but miss the model specifically described for extended notes and computer use.
feedback.instructional: Compare every requirement, not just one. Claude Opus 4.5 matches the long-context, code, and computer-use combination.

options.error_type: Confuses efficient general use with frontier complex-agent work
options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 is a balanced general-purpose model. It is not the stated strongest fit for complex code and multi-step computer use.
options.better_fit: Choose Mistral Large 3 when quality, throughput, cost, and latency need balance.

feedback.intrinsic: The work could be selected mainly for balance when it needs the stated sophisticated-agent strengths.
feedback.instructional: Mistral is a practical general-purpose option. Claude Opus 4.5 is the better match for this demanding combination.

options.error_type: Confuses high-volume chat with sophisticated agent work
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is optimized for real-time, high-volume chat. The analyst’s work needs extended context and complex multi-step tasks.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-4.1 for fast, efficient interactive applications at scale.

feedback.intrinsic: The choice would optimize response speed rather than the depth of the research task.
feedback.instructional: Fast chat is different from long-context, complex-agent work. Choose Claude Opus 4.5 here.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Claude Opus 4.5 is the stated fit for all three requirements.

exercises.question_text: For high-volume production workloads that need fast responses, choose ___.

parts.text: For high-volume production workloads that need fast responses, choose

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The workload could be assigned to a model selected for deep reasoning, balanced general use, or complex long-context work instead of speed at scale.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use GPT-4.1 for the speed-and-scale clue. GPT-5.x emphasizes reasoning, Mistral balances trade-offs, and Claude Opus 4.5 fits complex long-context tasks.

exercises.explanation: GPT-4.1 is optimized for speed, efficiency, and low-latency inference. It is better suited than reasoning-heavy models for high-volume production workloads.

exercises.question_text: Foundation models are large pretrained models that can provide general capabilities out of the box.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice would rule out a ready-to-deploy base model for a general task.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundation models are large pretrained models. They can be deployed immediately or customized through fine-tuning.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Foundation models already provide general language, reasoning, or multimodal capabilities.

exercises.question_text: An education platform is launching a tutoring chat for many students at once. It needs fast, efficient replies, and deep multi-step reasoning is not the main need. Which model should the team choose?

options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is optimized for speed, efficiency, and low-latency inference. It is better suited than reasoning-heavy models for high-volume production workloads.

options.error_type: Confuses reasoning-heavy work with high-volume speed
options.rationale: GPT-5.x is designed for multi-step reasoning, structured logic, and planning. Deep reasoning is not the main need in this tutoring chat.
options.better_fit: Choose GPT-5.x when technical reports, planning, or accuracy-focused multi-step reasoning are central.

feedback.intrinsic: The platform could favor reasoning depth while many students mainly need quick replies.
feedback.instructional: Let the volume and response-time need drive the choice. GPT-4.1 is optimized for that workload.

options.error_type: Confuses frontier agent work with low-latency production
options.rationale: Claude Opus 4.5 fits sophisticated agents, complex code reasoning, and multi-step computer use. The tutoring chat instead needs efficient high-volume replies.
options.better_fit: Choose Claude Opus 4.5 for complex code, long specifications, or computer-use tasks.

feedback.intrinsic: The choice could optimize for complex tasks the tutoring chat does not primarily perform.
feedback.instructional: The scenario prioritizes speed at scale. GPT-4.1 is the model described for that priority.

options.error_type: Confuses balanced trade-offs with GPT-4.1 optimization
options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 balances quality, throughput, cost, and latency. GPT-4.1 is explicitly optimized for fast, efficient, low-latency production workloads.
options.better_fit: Choose Mistral Large 3 when a general-purpose workload needs balanced quality, cost, and latency.

feedback.intrinsic: The platform could settle for broad balance instead of the stated fast-chat optimization.
feedback.instructional: Both can consider response time, but GPT-4.1 is the direct fit for many fast tutoring-chat replies.

exercises.explanation: Correct. GPT-4.1 fits a high-volume tutoring chat where fast, efficient replies matter most.

exercises.question_text: GPT-5.x is available to all Foundry users without registration.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A team could plan around a model family before confirming that it is available to them.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: GPT-5.x currently requires registration. GPT-4.1 is the model stated as available to all Foundry users.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Registration currently restricts access to the GPT-5 model family.

exercises.question_text: A content team is choosing a model for campaign drafts in several languages. It needs strong quality but must keep throughput, cost, and response time balanced. Which reasons favor Mistral Large 3? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Mistral Large 3 is described as a general-purpose model. That makes it suitable for a broad campaign-drafting workload.
Efficient throughput is a stated strength of Mistral Large 3. It helps meet the team’s need to process work efficiently.
Mistral Large 3 is positioned around cost and latency trade-offs. The scenario explicitly requires that balance.

options.error_type: Confuses Mistral Large 3 with Claude Opus 4.5
options.rationale: Complex multi-step computer use is a stated fit for Claude Opus 4.5. Mistral Large 3 instead emphasizes balanced general-purpose work.
options.better_fit: Choose Claude Opus 4.5 for sophisticated agents, complex code reasoning, and multi-step computer use.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could choose based on a specialty it does not need, while missing the desired balance.
feedback.instructional: Use the requirements in the scenario. Mistral Large 3 is favored for quality with balanced throughput, cost, and latency.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These reasons explain why Mistral Large 3 fits a quality-focused workload with balanced trade-offs.

exercises.question_text: A software team is designing an agent that must coordinate a code-analysis tool and a document-search tool. Accuracy matters more than the fastest reply. Which reasons support choosing GPT-5.x? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: GPT-5.x is optimized for agentic workflows. Coordinating several capabilities is an agentic-workflow need.
GPT-5.x supports adjustable thinking levels. They allow a speed-for-accuracy trade-off.

options.text: It is optimized for multi-step reasoning
options.rationale: GPT-5.x is optimized for multi-step reasoning. The agent must reason across more than one action.

options.text: It is best for low-latency volume
options.rationale: GPT-4.1 is optimized for low-latency, high-volume production. That is not the priority in this scenario.
options.better_fit: Use GPT-4.1 when a large number of fast chat replies is the main requirement.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could optimize the wrong priority and weaken the case for careful multi-step work.
feedback.instructional: When accuracy and coordinated reasoning matter most, GPT-5.x has the stated strengths.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The selected reasons all connect GPT-5.x to careful, multi-step agent work.

exercises.question_text: Large pretrained models such as GPT, Claude, and Mistral are called ___.

parts.text: Large pretrained models such as GPT, Claude, and Mistral are called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The term would describe either a broader category, one family, or a catalog source instead of this base-model type.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use “foundation model.” A language model is broader, GPT-5.x is one family, and Azure-direct describes a source.

exercises.explanation: This name identifies large pretrained models that provide broad capabilities before customization. GPT, Claude, and Mistral are listed as examples.
